output.best_reason: Version B has the most distinct voice and the most tension. Lina's refusal to sit ("I will stand, if it is the same to you") and her line "I would not put a theory into a clock, and I will not put one into your notebook" establish her character quickly. Matthey's probing follow-ups ("You were watching the clock closely") build pressure, and the detail that she helped with the hairsprings and knows what the work cost him gives the repeater an emotional weight the facts don't need to state outright. Its one overreach is "I was waiting for something, though I did not know what," which tells the reader what to feel. Version A is close behind: "He was well. I want you to write that down exactly" and the closing "Please write it correctly" are strong, and its period texture is convincing. Its repeater explanation reads more like a recital. Version C is the most efficient and gives the clock readings cleanly, and "It is only a fact, like a reading" is a good line. But its tight question-and-answer rhythm turns the facts into an interrogation checklist, so the voice feels less lived-in than in A or B.
